subject: Renewal pathway: 8→16 GPUs and revised monthly commit
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novusai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pathway: 8→16 GPUs and revised monthly commit

Hi Sarah —

Hope you had a great weekend. As NovusAI’s renewal window approaches (term ends 2026-09-30), I wanted to lay out a straightforward pathway we discussed in our last QBR: moving from your current 8-GPU reserved pool to a 16-GPU reserved pool for the next term.

High-level proposal: 
- Target start: 2026-10-01 (new term)
- Reserved capacity: 16 GPUs (upgrade from 8)
- Suggested monthly commit (reserved spend): increase from your current $65,000/mo to $120,000/mo to match 16-GPU reserved pricing and throughput SLA
- SLA: committed throughput baseline with a 99th percentile latency SLO; we can include a canary period for the first 30 days.

Why this path? it gives Novus predictable throughput for peak inference windows and a 25–35% cost-per-token improvement vs. on-demand burst usage we’ve seen in your org. We’ll provide a phased migration plan (zero-downtime KV cache migration, prefix-matching for gradual traffic shift) and a short performance validation window so your engineering team can verify latency and tails.

If this looks good, I’ll route an amendment for signature and include a detailed throughput table and proposed phasing schedule. Are you available for a quick call Thursday 8/6 to walk the plan with procurement and infra?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: none in this note (I will attach amendment + SLA table next).

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novusai.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pathway: 8→16 GPUs and revised monthly commit

Thanks Mateo — quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement into a formal review.

1) Term length: do you propose a 12- or 24-month contract? We prefer 12 for flexibility but need to understand price delta.
2) Billing cadence: can billing be monthly with a mid-term reconciliation? Procurement needs an itemized amendment for their system.
3) SLA specifics: can you share the exact throughput numbers and what constitutes an SLA breach (measured over what window)?
4) Migration: what does the phased ramp look like operationally — will there be any packet loss/traffic errors during prefix switch?

We’re targeting our internal budget signoff on 8/20; if we can get a clean amendment and a short migration runbook, procurement can fast-track.

Cc’ing procurement for visibility.

—Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Platform, NovusAI
sarah.chen@novusai.com

Rishi / Laura — forwarding Sarah’s reply (below). Key asks: term length, itemized amendment for procurement, explicit throughput/SLA numbers, and a migration runbook.

My read: Novus prefers a 12-month term if the pricing delta is reasonable. They want monthly billing with reconciliation. They also want a clear migration plan (no traffic loss).

Suggested approach: 
- Offer 12-month term with an option to extend at a tiered discount in month 10 if they want to lock 24 months.
- Monthly billing with a quarterly reconciliation clause for overages/credits.
- Throughput SLA: propose a baseline guaranteed aggregate throughput equivalent to 16 GPUs at 75% utilization with a 99th percentile tail latency SLO; specify measurement window (5-minute rolling windows aggregated daily).
- Migration: 30-day phased ramp (10/01–10/30) with canary at 10% traffic for first 72 hours, then 50% for a week, then full switch; ops playbook + rollback plan.

If you confirm pricing I’ll schedule a short call Thurs 8/6 with Sarah + procurement to run through.

—Mateo

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@novusai.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RDW amendment v3: NovusAI 8→16 GPU upgrade + monthly commit (proposal)

Sarah — attaching amendment (redwood_amendment_v3.pdf) and a short throughput/SLA breakdown (throughput-sla-table.csv) per your ask. TL;DR on commercials: 

- Term: 12 months (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30)
- Reserved capacity: 16 GPUs (dedicated reserved pool)
- Monthly commit: $120,000/mo (reflects reserved pricing for 16 GPUs); current: $65,000/mo
- Billing: monthly invoicing with quarterly reconciliation for consumption beyond commit; overage credits applied pro-rata
- SLA: baseline aggregate throughput guaranteed (equivalent to sustained aggregate token throughput of 1.2e7 tokens/day at 99th percentile latency < 250ms for single-token generations). Breach definition: measured over rolling 5-minute windows aggregated hourly; remedies include service credits per amendment schedule.
- Migration: 30-day phased ramp with canary (10% traffic first 72 hours), validation checklist, and a rollback trigger if error rates exceed 0.5% above baseline.

I’ve also included a recommended operational addendum for a 30-day canary and an optional 90-day performance validation (we can absorb a one-time validation lab run). If this looks good, we’ll send via DocuSign for signature (link included).

Attachments:
- redwood_amendment_v3.pdf (PDF, 28KB)
- throughput-sla-table.csv (CSV, 3KB)

Next steps: if Novus is aligned, we’ll send the DocuSign packet and schedule an ops kickoff for the week of 9/27 to prepare for the 10/01 start.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
